---
title: "A14 Methodological case reports or case series"
link-citations: true
---

## Definition and features
In methodological case reports, researchers describe their experience with the design, implementation, or performance of a method in one real study, typically their own. In methodological case series, researchers discuss two or more studies that share a similar method or methodological challenge.

- A strength is that they can provide detailed practical insights.
- A limitation is that their findings may not generalize to other settings.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## Boundaries with related types
[Experimental analyses of real datasets](3real-datasets.qmd) and [informal approaches](15informal.qmd): All may use a single dataset and the label "case study". Key differences are that A3 re-analyzes an existing dataset to answer a methodological question, A14 discusses methodological challenges in a specific study, and A15 uses datasets or studies to illustrate methods.

[Reviews of applied or planned methods](9review-applied.qmd): While a case series is a narrative aggregating teams' experience with a method, a review of applied or planned methods answers a methodological question by analyzing published study reports.
:::

## Typical objectives and corresponding examples
[Evaluate a single method](../objectives/7evaluate-method.qmd): experience with using large language models to develop a clinical practice guideline;[@Sousa-Pinto2024-gz] lessons learned from applying a framework to develop a healthcare intervention;[@Lindblom2025-ez] challenges and benefits of including non-randomized evidence in living systematic reviews;[@Bonnet2026including] demonstration of target trial emulation.[@Martinuka2023target]
